For the test project, do this:

1. Click a contig's ID to open it, and look over its features and checks.
2. Close the window, then tick every row with the box in the table header.
3. Press **Lock**. The app asks about CHIM01, which is flagged; choose **Lock
   anyway**.

Contigs must be locked here before they can be exported. The rest of this page
explains what you are looking at.

Each kept contig of a locked sample is one row:

![The Annotation Review table, one row per contig](figures/get-started/annotation-table.png)

The **Checks** column sums up each contig's checks as in the Assemble step. It sits
right after the ID, or after **Path #** and **Contig #** when a sample has more
than one contig, as in the test project. The Warnings, ITSx Warnings, Screen, and
Chimera columns further right hold the details; the **Columns** menu shows or
hides them under **Check details**.

Click a contig's ID to open it. The window shows the feature model (18S, ITS1,
5.8S, ITS2, 28S), **Sequence and read coverage**, **Edit active feature
boundaries**, the **Reference alignment**, **Curation warnings**, the
**Chimera check**, and **Notes**. Your notes also show in the table's **User
Notes** column once you close the window.

**Sequence and read coverage** draws the contig as a zoomable map: read depth,
the share of reads clipped at each base, the genes as arrows (dashed ends are
partial), and the bases once you zoom in. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, or type a
position. Clicking a gene makes it the active feature, the one that **Edit
active feature boundaries** and the **Reference alignment** act on.

![A contig: its five features, read coverage, and gene map](figures/get-started/annotation-details.png)

Three marks record what you decided about a contig: **Mark Reviewed**, **Exclude
& Lock**, and **Mark Partial**. Use the toolbar buttons for the ticked contigs, or
the buttons at the top of a contig's window.
[Preparing a GenBank submission](GenBank-Submission.html#check-before-you-submit)
says what each mark does to the export.

**Lock** locks the contig and keeps the window open; **Lock & Close** locks it and
closes the window. Neither marks it Reviewed. If the contig has a red Checks
finding and is not marked Reviewed, both ask first, as **Lock** in the toolbar
does.

A locked contig is read only. To change its boundaries, trim it, restore it, or
change its marks, unlock it first. Only contigs that are locked here, and whose
sample is locked in the Assemble step, can be exported. Only one assembly path
can be locked per sample: paths are alternative reconstructions of the same
rDNA repeat, and a sample exports one. If a sample shows contigs from more than
one path, lock the contigs of its **Selected Path** (see the Assemble table)
unless the checks point to another.

GenBank tends to reject sequence outside the genes, so trim before a real
submission. To trim many contigs at once, tick them and press **Trim** in the toolbar. Choose
**Match gene ends** to keep only the span from 18S to 28S, or **Gene
ends + flank** to keep a few extra bases on each side. Only contigs
with all five features (18S, ITS1, 5.8S, ITS2, and 28S) are trimmed; the window
lists the others and why, such as a missing feature or a lock, before you
confirm. While a run is going, contigs still queued in it are skipped. **Restore** next to it undoes the trim on the ticked contigs, as
**Restore assembly** does in a contig's window.

Changes here apply at once: a trim or a boundary edit re-checks the contig right
away. Press **Update** in the Assemble step again only after you change an
option set, or set a State to Ready to run.

[Quality checks and flags](Curation-Flags.html) explains what each warning
means.
